79c112ac12d89cc4c2881a3b23c05b5eb05fbc98.summary: A BlackBerry Research & Intelligence Team write-up on emulating a macOS ARM64 kernel under QEMU on a Linux host, to reach an interactive shell for debugging and vulnerability research by pen-testers and researchers. It describes a methodology and project log. It names no threat actor, malware family, campaign, incident, sector, country or CVE, so it is not a threat report.

audit_history.note: summary: Says it describes 'macOS 11 ARM64e kernel' and 'reaching a shell' fine, but claims it is aimed at 'debugging and vulnerability discovery' for pen-teste

798de1d888a708ba10b2739e34a9f7ca980bb2cd.summary: News report from The Register dated 14 Sep 2011 on Trojan.Mebromi, a rootkit that reflashes a computer's BIOS chip to add malicious code. The code alters the master boot record and checks the BIOS on each boot, so it survives antivirus removal. Per Webroot's researcher, it only targets Award BIOS ROMs and was first documented by Qihoo 360, mainly infecting machines in China. The report also mentions earlier BIOS-modifying malware (CIH/Chernobyl in the late 1990s, IceLord in 2007). Much of the page is unrelated news teasers.
